name: Isfahan
literature_vertical_cm_per_yr: -5 to -11 across Isfahan-Borkhar plain (localized hotspots up to -14 to -25)
literature_sources: Esmaeili et al. / Motagh et al. Isfahan-Borkhar Sentinel-1 PSI & SBAS InSAR studies
Iranian geological & Zayandeh-Rud groundwater subsidence assessments (2025-2026)
agreement_note: 120-day LOS peak (-2.5 cm LOS; -3.4 cm vertical est., ~-10.3 cm/yr vertical est.) sits squarely within the published -5 to -11 cm/yr Isfahan-Borkhar range. Two southern rocky-margin references (51.589E, 32.355N and 51.949E, 32.414N) agree tightly (-2.5 to -2.6 cm), whereas alt_ref 2 (51.697E, 32.805N) sits near the northern Borkhar subsidence peak and pulls the headline to -0.8 cm. Valid fraction is 32.5%.
press_summary_gate_note: Consistent with published -5 to -11 cm/yr range when referenced to southern rocky foothills; label as provisional 120-day estimate (valid_fraction 32.5%).

first_nisar_measurement.evidence: No peer-reviewed or official NASA/ISRO NISAR subsidence publication found for Isfahan as of 2026-11-14.
first_nisar_measurement.atlas_first_claim_note: Multi-basin standardized atlas phrasing must use qualified (to our knowledge) only after excluding Mexico City from any individual-first claim.

quality_note: NISAR data are provisional. Calibration and validation are carried out by the NISAR project (NASA-JPL and ISRO), not by our team.
